account:
Today I heard a vague rumour of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' The neighbour attributed those words to Townsfolk Two, whom they met outside the bakery around ten this morning. When pressed, the neighbour said the supporting observations were merely the baker carrying wheat and lights at the bakery. The neighbour had not seen gatherings or interesting visitors at the docks, and reported that the baker described his work as ordinary fresh-bread baking. I have not spoken directly with Townsfolk Two about it. There is no confirmed riverside project in what I have learned; ordinary baking could explain those observations.

The innkeeper has invited me to a community hospitality presentation tomorrow at eighteen in the town hall's great hall, involving the inn and local tradespeople and showcasing local baking and hospitality. I accepted. This may explain some activity involving baking, but I have no evidence connecting it to the rumour or showing any hidden purpose. The innkeeper said no preparation is needed from me.

Town administration has also revealed missing financial information: the treasury contains 128 emeralds, but no ledger or obligations records were there, and the secretary does not know where previous accounts were kept. That is an unresolved records problem, not evidence of missing money. I gave the secretary one personal emerald to buy a writable book for the additional appointment and cash-count report, since the signed appointment book cannot be amended. The secretary subsequently requested funding again despite holding the emerald; my attempted clarification reached nobody. I have now returned home for my nineteen-o'clock appointment. Tomorrow I should read my appointment book in the morning and keep the scheduled mill grain inspection as well as the newly agreed presentation.
